attempts.text: Iterative critique can improve the score used to refine a model explanation, but that improvement need not transfer to another operationalization of faithfulness. It may instead reflect metric-specific optimization, ordinary re-prompting instability, or sensitivity to added text. Existing work already introduces self-refinement, intervention-guided optimization, prediction–explanation consistency metrics, and causal tests of faithfulness measures. The defensible gap is narrower: whether refinement gains survive a held-out metric and exceed specificity controls. We propose a paired audit on natural-language inference and fact verification using two model families. For each initially correct prediction, we will compare the original explanation with self-critique, metric-guided critique, external critique, and a neutral rewrite at one and three rounds. The refinement metric will be separated from held-out intervention and consistency measures. Content-free filler, unrelated-text, and answer re-injection controls will estimate nonspecific answer-change floors. Prediction accuracy, valid-output coverage, explanation length, and blinded human ratings of clarity—not faithfulness—will remain separate outcomes. The proposed contribution is a falsifiable replication-and-extension protocol for distinguishing transferable faithfulness improvement from metric alignment.
